summary: Optimizing LLM usage at inference time can cut API spend by 50-90% while improving latency, often reducing monthly bills from thousands to hundreds of dollars without sacrificing output quality. The highest-leverage techniques are prompt caching (up to 90% input cost savings), semantic caching (60-70% hit rates), and model routing/cascading that sends simple queries to cheaper models. Combining several techniques compounds savings and is standard practice in production AI systems.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse previously processed static portions of a prompt (system instructions, few-shot examples, documents) so the provider charges a reduced rate for cached tokens instead of reprocessing them each call.
techniques.savings: up to 90% reduction on repeated input tokens
techniques.example: Place a large, unchanging system prompt and document context at the start of every request so Anthropic/OpenAI serve those tokens from cache at a fraction of the input price on subsequent calls.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by the semantic meaning (embedding similarity) of a query rather than exact string match, so paraphrased repeat questions return cached answers without hitting the model.
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to detect that 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset steps?' are near-identical and serve the stored response instead of a new completion.

techniques.name: Model Routing / Cascading
techniques.description: Route each query to the cheapest capable model, escalating to larger models only when a small model's confidence or validation fails.
techniques.example: Send simple classification or FAQ queries to GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku, and only escalate to GPT-4o or Claude Opus when the cheaper model returns low-confidence or malformed output.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Optimization
techniques.description: Trim redundant wording, shorten few-shot examples, remove boilerplate, and compress context to reduce the number of input tokens sent per request.
techniques.example: Replace verbose multi-paragraph instructions with concise bullet directives and use tools like LLMLingua to compress long contexts while preserving meaning.

techniques.name: Output Token Limiting
techniques.description: Cap max_tokens and instruct the model to be concise or return structured/short formats, since output tokens are typically priced higher than input tokens.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens appropriately and add 'Respond in JSON with only the fields requested' to avoid long, rambling completions.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over Stuffing
techniques.description: Retrieve only the most relevant chunks via vector search and inject them, instead of stuffing entire documents into every prompt.
techniques.example: Instead of pasting a 50-page manual, embed it and retrieve the 3 most relevant passages to answer a user's specific question.

techniques.name: Request Batching
techniques.description: Group multiple independent tasks into a single call or use provider batch APIs that offer discounted asynchronous processing.
techniques.savings: up to 50% via batch API discounts
techniques.example: Submit a large set of non-urgent classification jobs through OpenAI's Batch API to get ~50% off standard pricing with 24h turnaround.

techniques.name: Streaming and Early Termination
techniques.description: Stream responses and stop generation as soon as the needed answer is produced, reducing wasted output tokens and perceived latency.
techniques.example: Stream tokens and abort the request once a stop sequence or complete JSON object is detected rather than waiting for max_tokens.

techniques.name: Fine-tuned Smaller / Open-Source Models
techniques.description: Replace frequent calls to expensive frontier models with a smaller or self-hosted open model tuned for your narrow task.
techniques.example: Host Llama 3.1 8B or Mistral on Groq/Fireworks for a repetitive extraction task instead of calling GPT-4o millions of times.

techniques.name: Quantization (self-hosted)
techniques.description: Run models at lower precision (INT8/INT4) to cut GPU memory and inference cost while retaining most accuracy.
techniques.example: Serve a 4-bit quantized model with vLLM to fit on cheaper GPUs and double throughput for the same hardware budget.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic cache for LLM queries that stores and retrieves responses by embedding similarity to avoid duplicate API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted; you pay only infra)

tools.name: Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: Vector-based semantic caching layer using Redis to serve cached LLM responses for semantically similar prompts, reducing cost and latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Redis OSS free; Redis Cloud paid tiers from ~$5/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK to call 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, routing, fallback, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LiteLLM Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing caching, cost tracking, rate limiting, and request logging.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/mo

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt templating, and RAG utilities.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LangSmith paid plans from ~$39/user/mo

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression tool that reduces prompt length while retaining key information to cut input token costs.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway offering semantic caching, smart routing, load balancing, fallbacks, and observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine for self-hosted models with PagedAttention, continuous batching, and quantization support.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted infra cost only)

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API that routes requests across many model providers, enabling easy model cost comparison and fallback routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-per-token passthrough pricing with small routing fee

tools.name: Martian / RouteLLM
tools.description: Model routing frameworks that automatically direct queries to the cheapest capable model based on complexity.
tools.pricing_paid: RouteLLM open-source free; Martian commercial pricing on request

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching for your static system prompts and document context to cut repeated input costs by up to 90% with almost no code change.
Switch high-volume simple queries from frontier models (GPT-4o, Claude Opus) to cheaper small models (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku) for an instant 50-80% drop.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of your API to serve repeat/paraphrased questions without new completions.
Trim verbose prompts and set tight max_tokens plus 'be concise / return JSON only' instructions to reduce both input and pricier output tokens.
Route non-urgent bulk jobs through provider Batch APIs for roughly 50% off standard token pricing.
